key_insight: Physical activity shares substantial polygenic architecture with schizophrenia and Parkinson’s disease, despite negligible overall genetic correlations because shared variants have mixed effect directions.
clinical_relevance: These findings provide a genetic basis for investigating activity changes across neuropsychiatric disorders, but do not establish a clinical biomarker or treatment.
method: Enhanced objectively measured activity GWAS using self-reported activity GWAS.
Compared activity genetics with schizophrenia and Parkinson’s disease GWAS.
Assessed overlap using causal mixture modelling, local genetic correlations and conjunctional false discovery rate analysis.
evidence_signal: Analyses included objectively measured activity in 89,683 participants, schizophrenia in 53,386 cases and 77,258 controls, and Parkinson’s disease in 63,555 cases, 17,700 proxy cases and 1,746,386 controls; overall genetic correlations were negligible (rg −0.02 to 0.02; p > 0.05).
watch_item: Shared genetic architecture does not establish causality or validate activity-based clinical prediction; this is not an AI cancer drug discovery study.
paper_title: Polygenic overlap of physical activity with schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease
